items.title: Kenny Barron — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Warren Smith said – you know, a drummer, percussionist – “What do you think about me playing the melody on vibes with you?”

ctx.x: What was your concept? Did you get the call? Or did you already have a concept that you wanted to get recorded?

No, I didn’t have a concept. So I had to get music together. That was a big part of it, getting the music together. There were some originals. I think I recorded one of Freddie Waits’s songs, Al-Kifha. It just worked. I think we recorded at A&R Studios, maybe? I’m not sure. Yeah, I think A&R Studios. That was the very first record date as a leader. There was one before that. It was co-led, I think, with Jimmy Owens, called You Had Better Listen. But that was as co-leader. That was fun to do. One of the things I…
I know you played some electric piano with Buddy Rich too, I think.
